The FFT node's table back to a signal.

Rebuilds the signal from the FFT node's real and imag columns (numpy.fft.irfft) as a new table with one column, signal, of `samples` rows (0: the even length 2 (bins - 1)). What comes back is the signal the FFT node transformed: windowed and mean-removed as it was.

| | |
| --- | --- |
| Category | [Signal](../categories/signal.md) |
| Status | Runs |
| Also read from graphs as | `IFFTNode` |
| Search words | ifft, inverse, fourier |

## Inputs

| Pin | Type | Required | Connections | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **Spectrum** | Dataset | Yes | 1 | The FFT node's table (real, imag) |

## Outputs

| Pin | Type | Required | Connections | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **Signal** | Dataset | Yes | 1 | One column, signal |

## Settings

| Setting | Key | Type | Default | Allowed values | Read by | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| samples | `samples` | Integer | `0` | `>= 0` | The run | The length of the signal the spectrum came from (0: 2 (bins - 1)) |

**Read by** says whether a run uses the setting (**The run**) or only the editor, a dialog or a view (**The editor only**).

## Where it runs

| Where | Runs |
| --- | --- |
| Data pipeline (run the graph, **Run step**, previews) | Yes; the result can be saved as a table |

The node runs on the device chosen for the run (CPU or a GPU); a node does not fix a device.
